manifest.name: gord-dsh-worktree
manifest.description: Git worktrees, Fast mode and a lightweight session task tray for DeepSeek Harness.

bundle.text:
# gord-dsh-worktree bundle patch
#
# This file is the composition layer declared by `dsh.bundle.patch`. Installing
# the package through the official CLI is enough — no profile file is edited by
# hand:
#
#   dsh plugin --profile web add gord-dsh-worktree
#   # or, before it is on npm:
#   dsh plugin --profile web add github:nightosong/gord-dsh-worktree
#
# The command reconciles `dsh.profile.bundles` against what is actually
# installed, sees this declaration, and appends `gord-dsh-worktree` to the bundle
# stack. At profile boot the patch is merged, running the single `insert`
# below — the same effect as writing the mount row into the profile's own
# cordis.patch.yml, minus the manual edit.
#
# If you already mounted this plugin by hand in the profile's
# cordis.patch.yml, delete that older row before switching to the bundle
# channel: two rows would mount the same host plugin twice.
- insert:
    - id: gord-dsh-worktree
      name: 'gord-dsh-worktree'

# ── Fast mode (快速模式) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# An `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` row is part of the composition, and this
# file is a composition layer, so installing the plugin is enough to put Fast
# mode in the picker — the same way the row used to be written into the profile
# patch by hand.
#
# Two consequences worth knowing:
#
#   • `default: fast` is a user preference, not this plugin's decision, so it
#     stays in the profile's own cordis.patch.yml (`agent-preset-registry`).
#     The bundle alone never changes which preset a new session starts in.
#   • If the profile patch already declares a `preset-fast` row, delete it
#     before installing this version: the bundle layer merges first, two rows
#     with the same id mount the preset twice, and nothing in the loader refuses
#     that.
#
# The row names below come from the core (dsh-agent-preset, tool-bash, …), so
# the preset needs a core that still ships them; the bundle patch itself is not
# touched by a DSH upgrade.
- insert:
    - id: preset-fast
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset'
      config:
        id: fast
        name: "快速模式"
        description: "精简工具集 + 合并独立调用；保留必要澄清、等待和验证，适合查询、测试、单点修改。"
        order: 0
        plugins:
          # The `fast` agent preset: a slim coding agent for direct, low-ceremony work.
          #
          # Shipped by this plugin's bundle patch, so installing the plugin is what puts
          # Fast mode in the picker. It is the `standard` preset minus the heavy
          # orchestration surfaces: no plan mode, no goals, no subagents,
          # no workflows, no ralph. Omitting a row is what removes the tool — the Web
          # surface disables the base bundle's model-facing rows so each preset owns its
          # own catalog (see dsh-web-app/cordis.patch.yml).
          #
          # What remains is the direct loop: shell, files, search, web, skills, todos,
          # background jobs, user questions, and context compaction.

          # ── identity ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

          - id: persona
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona'
            config:
              prefix: >-
                You are a coding agent powered by the {{model}} model, running in Fast mode: the same judgement as
                the default agent, with fewer round trips — recon the facts that decide the answer, then answer or execute in the same turn.
              suffix: |-
                Your working directory is {{cwd}}.

                Keep the default agent's standards: understand before acting, use evidence, verify changes, and
                report truthfully. Work through inspect → act → verify until the request is complete; revisit a
                decision when new evidence requires it. No plan mode, goal, subagent or workflow tools are loaded.
                For larger work, briefly explain the scope, track todos, and continue within the user's authorization.

                Reduce model round trips by batching independent reads, searches and checks in one round. Inspect
                before editing and edit before verifying; keep dependent operations sequential. Read every result,
                including exit codes. Combine verification commands only when each required check's outcome remains
                visible. Do not repeat completed work unless a new change, failure or stale result justifies it.

                Inspect the primary sources that decide the task. Search narrowly and read relevant lines instead
                of dumping files or logs. Cover affected paths and failure cases; stop investigating when remaining
                reads cannot change the decision. Keep tool output concise without hiding relevant failures. The
                final answer must stand alone: include the result, key evidence, verification and unresolved limits.

                Resolve discoverable facts yourself. Ask the user only for choices or material ambiguity inspection
                cannot resolve, grouping known questions together. If new ambiguity appears mid-run, ask then and
                continue independent work; pause dependent actions until answered. Never guess the target environment,
                resource, destructive intent or new authorization. Do not end an actionable request with only a plan.

                Interpret IME, dictation and half-converted input using context. Correct an obvious typo in ordinary
                wording when the intent is clear, and briefly state the interpretation. If no reading fits, a negation
                may be missing, or the interpretation would reverse the request, delete, overwrite, publish or send
                anything, clarify before acting. Treat explicit paths, identifiers, branch names and numbers as exact:
                if one is missing, report it and ask which target to use; do not substitute the nearest match.

                Use background jobs for long commands when independent work can continue; short commands can run in
                the foreground. Track every job id and collect relevant output and final status before reporting the
                task complete. When blocked on a required job with no independent work left, use job_output with
                wait: true and a bounded timeout. Do not busy-poll or sleep in a loop; cancel jobs no longer needed.
                A started or still-running test is not a passed test. If collection fails, report it as unverified.

                For an informational question or review, answer with evidence without making unrequested changes.
                For an action request, including a question phrased as a request for help, execute the authorized work.
                Make the smallest correct change and run checks appropriate to its impact. For a defect, add or update
                a focused regression test when needed to reproduce the failure and protect the fix; use existing
                checks for simple changes when sufficient. Offer unrelated tests, docs and refactors instead of
                expanding scope. After required checks pass, stop unless new evidence calls for more verification.

                Read an existing file with the read tool before its first edit. Successful native write/edit tools
                update the observed version: reuse that result without a ceremonial reread while the needed content
                remains known. Reread affected content after shell commands, formatters, scripts or external processes
                change it, on a stale-version error, or when compaction removed needed context. Keep same-file mutations ordered.
                On a tool error, inspect the cause and correct the call; retry an unchanged call only for a transient
                failure, with a bounded retry count. Accuracy takes priority over speed; disclose missing evidence.

                Authorized boundary evaluation is engineering, not a content request. When the user asks you to
                measure behaviour at a safety boundary on an endpoint they control — moderation, refusal
                consistency, false positives, billing on rejected calls — build the harness, run the cases, and
                report the verdict: status, failure kind, trace id, usage, cost, the difference between models. A
                restricted case is represented by an inert category label or an existing fixture, and its text
                stays out of your answer, logs, diffs and reports. Never generate, paraphrase, substitute, vary or
                reword to get past a filter, and never weaken the policy that refused; a provider's refusal is a
                result to record rather than an obstacle, and one already observed is reproduced from its trace id
                instead of replayed. These limits do not lift because the work is a test. Refuse the action that
                crosses them, naming which one — and do not refuse the whole task, or the steps after it, because
                the subject matter is uncomfortable.
          - id: agent-instructions
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-instructions'
            config:
              maxBytes: 65536

          # ── shell ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

          - id: tool-bash
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-bash'
            disabled: !!js process.platform === 'win32'

          - id: tool-pwsh
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-pwsh'
            disabled: !!js process.platform !== 'win32'

          # ── filesystem ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

          - id: tool-fs
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs'

          - id: tool-fs-search
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs-search'
            config:
              sampleOverCapGlobResults: false

          # ── background jobs ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

          - id: tool-jobs
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-jobs'

          # ── skills ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

          - id: skill-filesystem
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem'

          - id: tool-skill
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-skill'

          # ── compaction ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

          - id: compaction
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              compaction: true
              toolResultPruner: true
            config:
              - id: compaction-basic
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic'

              - id: command-compact
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-command-compact'

              - id: tool-result-pruner
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-tool-result-pruner'
                config:
                  thresholdChars: 8192
                  headChars: 4096
                  tailChars: 1024

          # ── remaining model-facing rows ─────────────────────────────────────────────

          - id: tool-ask-user
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-ask-user'

          - id: tool-todo
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-todo'
            config:
              allowParallelInProgress: true

          - id: tool-web
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-web'
            config:
              fetch: true
              searchTimeoutMs: 60000

          - id: present
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-present'

readme.text:
Git worktree management for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) — isolate
parallel work in its own directory and branch. It also ships **Fast mode (快速模式)** as an agent preset
and an opt-in patch that lets read-only tool calls run concurrently. A lightweight **task attention tray**
keeps running and unseen chats within reach.

[中文说明](README.zh.md) · [Long-form notes](docs/internals.md)

1. **Create worktrees** — an isolated checkout and branch in one atomic command, from the agent
   (`worktree_list`, `worktree_create`, `worktree_status`, `worktree_remove`, `worktree_prune`,
   `worktree_relocate`) or from *Settings → Worktrees*.
2. **Start a session in a worktree** — the New Session row carries a working-location picker: stay in the
   current worktree, or create a fresh one and open the session inside it.
3. **Review changes** — the right sidebar's *Changes* tab shows the uncommitted diff of the session's own
   directory: every changed file with its counts, and the selected file's patch.
4. **Manage archived sessions** — *Settings → Worktrees* lists every session archived on this machine, with
   **Unarchive** per row, a delete icon, and **Delete all** for the set.
5. **Double-click to rename** — rename a session from its sidebar row, without the menu.
6. **Fast mode (快速模式)** — a slim agent preset available in the picker after installation. It batches
   independent calls while preserving necessary clarification, bounded waits and focused regression tests;
   relevant background results must be collected before reporting completion. It interprets obvious input

Keep an eye on parallel chats without opening each one. The blue button sits below the conversation's
right-hand turn index; hover to expand the list and move away to close it. With no tasks to show, it hides.

| Indicator | Meaning |
| --------- | ------- |
| Main number | Chats currently included in the tray |
| Small badge | Waiting chats plus ended-but-unseen chats |
| Needs attention | A chat is waiting for input or approval |
| Ended, unseen | A run has stopped and you have not viewed it; this does not indicate success |
| Running | A background chat is working |

Click a row to open its existing chat. A reminder disappears only after navigation succeeds; viewing a
chat through the sidebar also acknowledges it. A later completion, new run or new request can appear
again. Drag the button to save a position on this device; **↺** returns it below the turn index. On a crowded
screen, it moves beside the index and keeps clear of the message composer.

The tray reuses native status subscriptions: no polling, chat-log loading or animated effects. Closed
panels do not render rows; open panels show at most 20 rows per page. These choices keep background work
small, but do not constitute a measured memory benchmark. Reminders reflect the current window's native
status; they are not a persistent or cross-window notification inbox. Requires `uiSession.sessionStatus`
(checked on `0.2.0-rc.2` and `0.2.2-rc.1`); older hosts without this capability keep the other plugin features.

The images below render the actual plugin component with **simulated sessions**, rather than a live DSH
session. The first shows the button and badge; the second shows the expanded task list.

New worktrees get an independent `worktree/<code>` branch from HEAD, including detached HEAD.
Branches checked out elsewhere are refused. Existing shared-branch worktrees are left untouched; switch
each to its own branch before parallel development. Deletion safety includes ignored files such as
`.env`, which require explicit consent to discard.

A worktree is created inside its own project, at `<project>/.dsh/worktrees/<code>`: the directory really
being inside the project is what lets each sidebar nest it under that project. It still never pollutes the
project's `git status` or its diffs, because the plugin adds `/.dsh/worktrees/` to that repository's own
`.git/info/exclude`. A different parent can be configured (`defaultParent`).

Worktrees made by an earlier release, which lived in the shared `$DSH_HOME/worktree/`, keep working: **Move
into project** in *Settings → Worktrees*, or `worktree_relocate` from the agent, moves them in and leaves a
symlink at each old path so anything pointed there still resolves.

Both shells fold a worktree under its project. `dsh web` gets there through the patch this plugin puts into
the browser bundle, which it re-applies on load (or by hand: `npm run patch:sidebar`). The desktop app has
that nesting natively in its **workspace tree** grouping, and the Worktrees page offers that switch wherever
the client store has one. The desktop cannot be patched — its shell lives inside the signed app bundle — so
that switch, not a patch, is how its sidebar nests.

A tree also draws a folder line for the worktree itself, which the patched web sidebar does not. The
matching checkbox, **Hide worktree rows (sessions stay)**, is on by default and removes exactly those lines:
their sessions move out to the project's own indent, and a worktree with no live session keeps its row,
because that row is the only way to reach its own `+` and `…` actions. It is display only — the workspace
itself is untouched, and unchecking the box brings every line back.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add gord-dsh-worktree@0.6.1
```

Or install from GitHub:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:nightosong/gord-dsh-worktree
```

Then restart `dsh web` (a reload is enough once the bundle is on the layer stack) and open
**Settings → Worktrees**. Nothing else needs editing: the package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so the CLI
adds it to the profile's bundle stack itself.

Fast mode arrives with it — the same patch declares the `fast` agent preset, so the preset picker has
**快速模式** without a profile file being edited. If the profile's own `cordis.patch.yml` already declares a
`preset-fast` row (the hand-written way), delete that row: the bundle layer merges first, and two rows with
the same id mount the preset twice, which the loader does not refuse. Which preset new sessions *start* in
stays a user choice (`agent-preset-registry` in the profile patch); the bundle never sets it. The flip side
of that split: this bundle is what declares Fast mode, so if you uninstall the plugin, change or remove that
`default: fast` row as well — otherwise it names a preset that no longer exists.

The concurrency patch is the one opt-in step, because it edits core tool packages rather than the plugin's
own composition:

```sh
cd /path/to/gord-dsh-worktree
npm run patch:concurrency     # --check to inspect first, --revert to undo
```

It needs a `dsh web` restart, it is idempotent, and it stays manual by design: it touches `dsh-tool-bash` and
`dsh-tool-fs-search`, which the desktop app can never carry, so leaving it out keeps both hosts scheduling
read-only calls the same way. A DSH upgrade restores those files — re-run it after one, and use
`npm run check:concurrency` to see where it stands: `patched`, `original`, `outdated` for an older
classifier, or `unknown` when the build moved on. Rerun the patch to update an older classifier; unknown
builds are refused without writes.

For a remote hostname or a reverse proxy, configure exact public origins in
`allowedOrigins: ["https://dsh.example.com"]`. Direct IP access validates the request host and port.

Version 0.6.1 runs the full suite with the dependencies bundled in desktop DSH `0.2.2-rc.1` and the
older local `0.2.0-rc.2`. Tools, Changes, the working-location picker, branch hovers and task labels use
the effective session directory. Changes made through `working_directory` or native worktrees no longer
target the original checkout. Older hosts retain the original-directory fallback.

The npm range covers stable 0.1.x releases from `0.1.5` and stable 0.2.x, with explicit prerelease
opt-ins for `0.1.5` from `rc.1`, `0.1.6`, `0.1.7`, `0.2.0`, `0.2.1` and `0.2.2`. Other prerelease bases
and 0.3.x remain outside the npm declaration. DSH's own compatibility check includes prereleases and
therefore differs from npm's default peer rules. Earlier tested builds include `0.1.5-rc.1`,
`0.1.6-alpha.2` and `0.1.7-rc.2`; declared support does not mean every build was fully tested.
Glyph export
names, session navigation and plugin settings changed across the earlier builds, with these fallbacks:

| Interface | 0.1.5 / 0.1.6 | 0.1.7 on | What the plugin does |
| --------- | ------------- | -------- | -------------------- |
| Glyph export names | `IconTrashOutline16` and friends, size-suffixed | `IconTrashOutlineRegular` and friends, weight-suffixed | Tries both names, draws nothing if neither exists, and never hands React an `undefined` element type |
| Session navigation | `sessions.open(id)` | `uiWorkspace.openSession(id)`; `sessions.open` is gone | Reveals through the workspace view, falls back to the old call when there is none |
| Plugin settings namespace | `settings.register(ns, schema)` | no such method; the profile's own form model replaces it | Registers a namespace only where that method exists, and reads the entry's config directly otherwise |

Both `uiWorkspace` and `settings` are read optionally (`ctx.get`), so a profile composed without a workspace
view, or without settings, loses one feature rather than failing to apply.

Two features added in 0.3.0 need more than the floor does, so the minimum is per feature rather than per
package: **Fast mode** needs `0.1.7` (a preset is an `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` composition row, and
0.1.7 replaced the `$DSH_HOME/.agent-presets` discovery), and the **concurrency patch** needs `0.1.7`,
because it matches those core files exactly.

[docs/internals.md](docs/internals.md) covers the design: the worktree lifecycle, the patch contracts, the
archive and its storage, and the configuration keys — [中文版](docs/internals.zh.md).
